caption: LUM-1457 Windows key-release defect: a ConPTY run of the real pi.exe. crossterm's Win32 backend reports a `Release` record after every key press, and `App::translate_event` used to map both kinds to an InputEvent — so every keystroke ran its handler twice. Panels 2-4 are the A/B: the pre-fix binary renders `> aallpphhaa  bbeettaa` after typing `alpha beta`, and one Backspace deletes two characters. Panel 5 submits a draft and shows the reply landing exactly once. Captured with scripts/pty_capture_win.py on Windows 10 (ConPTY), 80x26.

expect.why: the composer starts empty with its placeholder

panels.label: 2. type `alpha beta`: one physical keystroke, one character

expect.why: the draft is exactly what was typed, caret at the end

reject.why: the pre-fix binary doubled every character (press + release both mapped). This row is a hard FAIL on that binary and the reason this scenario exists.
a doubled stream shows doubled text here too

expect.why: `bet` is gone; the trailing space is kept because the caret sits after it

panels.label: 5. Enter submits the draft once and the reply lands once

expect.why: the faux model's reply (`(faux) hello`, rendered as the dim provider label plus the reply text) landed, so the submit really reached the agent

reject.why: a doubled keystroke stream submits `hhii` instead of `hi`

panels.label: 6. the composer is empty again after the submit

expect.why: the draft was handed over, the placeholder is back
